name: Ω Interoperability Fabric
purpose: Give OMEGA standards-based boundaries for AI agents, digital credentials, IoT/robotics, spatial worlds and external services without coupling the core platform to a single vendor or protocol.

protocolFamilies.role: Expose governed tools and data to authorized agents.
protocolFamilies.policy: Every tool invocation requires identity, scope, authorization, audit event and failure semantics.

protocolFamilies.role: Allow OMEGA agents to communicate with compatible external agents through explicit task contracts.
protocolFamilies.policy: Remote agents are untrusted peers until identity, capability, scope and response provenance are verified.

protocolFamilies.role: Represent machine-verifiable claims such as education, skills, credentials and organizational attestations.
protocolFamilies.policy: Credential presentation must be purpose-limited and disclose only required claims.

protocolFamilies.role: Potential transport boundary for constrained device and sensor telemetry.
protocolFamilies.policy: Authentication, authorization, encryption, topic isolation and device identity are mandatory before production use.

protocolFamilies.role: Potential robotics adapter boundary for robot capabilities, telemetry and supervised commands.
protocolFamilies.policy: OMEGA never assumes that a ROS graph or robot command is safe merely because it is reachable.

protocolFamilies.role: Potential scene-description boundary for interoperable spatial worlds, assets, simulation and robotics visualization.
protocolFamilies.policy: Assets require validation, provenance and explicit separation between simulation and observed physical state.

protocolFamilies.role: Potential geospatial/digital-twin boundary for cities, regions and planetary visualization.
protocolFamilies.policy: Geospatial claims must retain source, timestamp, coordinate reference and freshness.

hardRules: No robot command is LIVE without device identity, authorization, safety state and result evidence.
No digital twin is physical truth unless backed by observed authoritative telemetry.
No external agent can escalate its own permissions.
No credential is accepted outside its stated issuer, subject, validity and purpose constraints.
Simulation and physical execution must remain visibly distinct.
